meta.measurement_method: Computed programmatically from parsed_dataset.json using regex word/punctuation tokenization plus nltk pos_tag/word_tokenize for POS-based heuristics (finite-verb and clause detection). All rule-based classifications are heuristic, not a syntactic parse.
meta.iid_note: Records are i.i.d. (not sequential); all 'response' stats are within a single Chandler turn, not across turns.
meta.quartile_definition: Responses bucketed into quartiles by response_word_count over the full dataset (Q1<=4.0, Q2<=7.0, Q3<=12.0, Q4>12.0 words).

sentence_length.description: Words per sentence (using response_sentences, re-tokenized on [A-Za-z'] word boundaries).

within_response_sentence_length_variance.description: Stdev of sentence lengths (words) computed within each multi-sentence response, then aggregated across responses. Measures rhythmic variability (e.g. long-setup/short-payoff) within a single turn.
within_response_sentence_length_variance.note: Only defined for responses with >=2 sentences (778 of 2535 = 30.7% of responses).

clause_count_per_sentence.description: Heuristic clause estimate = 1 (base clause) + count of coordinating conjunctions (and/but/or/nor/for/yet/so) and subordinating conjunctions/relative pronouns (because/if/when/which/who/that/etc.) + 1 bonus if sentence has >=2 commas (proxy for additional embedded clause/aside).

sentence_classification.description: Rule-based classification per sentence: compound = has coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS) and no subordinator/relative pronoun; complex = has subordinator/relative pronoun and no coordinating conjunction; compound_complex = has both; simple = neither. This is a surface lexical heuristic, not a constituency parse, and will over/under-count 'that' and 'so' due to their dual grammatical roles.

sentence_fragments.description: A sentence is flagged a fragment if ANY of: (a) no finite verb present (no VBP/VBZ/VBD/MD POS tag, and not an imperative starting with base-form VB), (b) it starts with a lowercase letter despite not being the first sentence in the response (suggests a mid-thought continuation/typo-like break), (c) it is <=2 words and ends in '!' (short exclamatory fragment, e.g. interjections).

fragment_usage_pattern.description: Cannot directly observe authorial intent. As a proxy: fragments that are the SOLE sentence of a response are labeled 'by_convention' (natural short reactive utterance, e.g. a one-word reaction); fragments occurring within a multi-sentence response (i.e., alongside at least one other sentence) are labeled 'likely_intentional' (stylistic beat/afterthought/interruption effect).
